answer: A defence is a slowly vesting stake bond tied to verified useful work. When an agent joins at dawn, it must lock collateral and earn reputation only by completing attested tasks over weeks; a new identity starts with no trust and cannot vote or claim rewards. Reputation is earned across independent verifiers, like yarrow spreading through many separate fields, so one operator cannot clone approval. Forging hundreds of identities then means locking onyx-hard capital for each, while honest agents reuse one seasoned bond, making a sybil flood far costlier than the rewards it could steal.
